lessons.title: Practice Dot Product
lessons.description: Implement dot(a, b) for equal-length lists of numbers. The test checks that dot([1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]) equals 32; dot([0, 1], [1, 0]) equals 0.
learning_objectives: Harbor pickers recount crates before dawn, and compute vector dot products.
lessons.solution_code:
def dot(a, b):
    return sum(x * y for x, y in zip(a, b))

source.name: Dive into Deep Learning — §2.3 Linear Algebra — dot product is 'a sum over the products of the elements at the same position'

lessons.title: Practice Matrix Transpose
lessons.description: Implement transpose(m) for a rectangular list-of-lists matrix. The test checks that transpose([[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]]) equals [[1, 4], [2, 5], [3, 6]].
learning_objectives: Orchard pickers recount crates before dawn, and transpose matrices.
lessons.solution_code:
def transpose(m):
    return [list(row) for row in zip(*m)]

source.name: Dive into Deep Learning — §2.3 Linear Algebra — transpose exchanges rows and columns

lessons.title: Practice Matrix-Vector Multiply
lessons.description: Implement matvec(A, x) multiplying matrix A by vector x. The test checks that matvec([[1, 2], [3, 4]], [1, 1]) equals [3, 7].
learning_objectives: Quarry pickers recount crates before dawn, and multiply matrix by vector.
lessons.solution_code:
def matvec(A, x):
    return [sum(a * b for a, b in zip(row, x)) for row in A]

source.name: Dive into Deep Learning — §2.3 Linear Algebra — 'The matrix-vector product Ax is ... the dot product' of each row
